title: Custom Rubber Compounding Services
subtitle: Engineered Elastomer Formulations for Demanding Applications
tagline: The right material makes the difference.
intro: SYNC Manufacturing provides custom rubber compounding services for OEMs requiring engineered elastomer materials with specific mechanical, thermal, chemical, and environmental performance characteristics.

Unlike manufacturers limited to commercially available rubber compounds, SYNC combines in-house formulation development, specialized mixing equipment, material testing, and precision molding expertise to create rubber solutions around the requirements of each application.

Our capabilities include custom elastomer formulation, compound modification, small-batch rubber mixing, material selection, developmental testing, and integration with compression molding, transfer molding, rubber-to-metal bonding, and industrial roller manufacturing.

Drawing upon more than 75 years of rubber engineering and manufacturing heritage, SYNC helps customers solve complex material challenges while supporting dependable production and long-term component performance.

blocks.text: Rubber compounding is the process of combining natural or synthetic elastomer polymers with carefully selected ingredients to achieve specific material properties.
A rubber compound typically contains a base elastomer along with reinforcing fillers, processing aids, curing agents, and other additives selected to achieve the desired performance.
The formulation determines how the rubber behaves during manufacturing and throughout its service life.

For example, two rubber compounds made from the same base polymer can exhibit significantly different hardness, tensile strength, compression set, abrasion resistance, chemical compatibility, and temperature performance.
Custom compounding allows these characteristics to be engineered around the intended application rather than relying entirely on standard material formulations.

items.title: Natural Rubber (NR)
body: Known for excellent resilience, elasticity, tensile properties, and dynamic performance.
Common applications include vibration isolators, industrial mounts, rollers, and mechanically demanding rubber components.

items.title: Nitrile Rubber (NBR)
body: Commonly selected for resistance to petroleum-based oils, fuels, and lubricants.
Applications include industrial seals, gaskets, rollers, and components exposed to compatible petroleum fluids.

items.title: EPDM
body: Offers strong resistance to weathering, ozone, water, and many outdoor environmental conditions.
Frequently used in utility equipment, industrial seals, protective components, and outdoor applications.

items.title: Neoprene (CR)
body: Provides balanced mechanical properties and resistance to weathering and selected industrial environments.
Used in protective components, seals, industrial equipment, and general-purpose rubber applications.

items.title: Silicone Rubber (VMQ)
body: Provides flexibility across a broad temperature range, excellent environmental aging characteristics, and useful electrical properties.
Common applications include specialized seals, insulation components, and precision silicone molded parts.

items.title: Styrene-Butadiene Rubber (SBR)
body: A versatile material offering abrasion resistance and general mechanical performance for industrial applications.

items.title: Fluoroelastomers (FKM)
body: Specialized materials selected for elevated-temperature performance and compatibility with certain aggressive chemicals, oils, and fuels.

items.title: Hydrogenated Nitrile Rubber (HNBR)
body: Offers enhanced temperature, oxidation, and mechanical performance compared with many conventional nitrile formulations.

items.title: Butyl Rubber (IIR)
body: Known for low gas permeability, environmental aging resistance, and specialized sealing properties.

items.title: Specialty Elastomers
body: Additional material families may include fluorosilicone, polyisoprene, polybutadiene, epichlorohydrin, acrylic elastomers, and specialty urethane compounds.
Material availability and processing suitability are evaluated according to application and manufacturing requirements.

blocks.text: The performance of a custom rubber component depends on more than the base polymer.
Compounding allows multiple material characteristics to be balanced to achieve the intended functional performance.

items.title: Mechanical Properties
body: Compounds can be developed around hardness, tensile strength, elongation, resilience, tear strength, abrasion resistance, and fatigue performance.

items.title: Temperature Resistance
body: Material formulations can be evaluated for elevated or reduced operating temperatures, thermal cycling, and long-term heat aging.

items.title: Chemical Resistance
body: Compound selection considers the specific fluids, concentrations, temperatures, and exposure conditions encountered during service.

items.title: Compression Set & Sealing Performance
body: Rubber formulations can be optimized for applications requiring deformation recovery, sealing force retention, and repeated compression.

items.title: Electrical Properties
body: Selected compounds can be formulated for electrical insulation, conductivity, or antistatic performance, depending on the base polymer and additive system.

items.title: Environmental Durability
body: Materials may be developed to address exposure to ozone, ultraviolet radiation, moisture, weathering, and other environmental factors.
The goal is to balance the characteristics required by the finished component rather than maximizing one property at the expense of others.

blocks.text: Developing the right rubber compound begins with understanding the application's performance requirements.

items.title: 1. Application & Specification Review
body: Our technical team evaluates drawings, material specifications, operating conditions, performance targets, and anticipated production requirements.

items.title: 2. Elastomer & Formulation Selection
body: We identify suitable base polymers, review existing compound options, and determine whether a new or modified formulation is appropriate.

items.title: 3. Development & Mixing
body: Selected ingredients are combined using controlled mixing processes to prepare material for evaluation and manufacturing trials.

items.title: 4. Material Evaluation & Refinement
body: Compound properties are evaluated against the application requirements. Where necessary, formulation adjustments are made to address performance or processing considerations.

items.title: 5. Manufacturing Integration
body: The selected compound is coordinated with the appropriate compression molding, transfer molding, bonding, or roller manufacturing process.

items.title: 6. Production & Quality Control
body: Approved formulations and relevant process requirements are used to support consistent production, material traceability, and customer-specific quality documentation.

items.title: Custom Rubber Rollers

items.q: What rubber materials can SYNC compound?
a: Our experience includes natural rubber, nitrile, EPDM, neoprene, silicone, SBR, FKM, and other specialty elastomers. Specific formulations are evaluated based on material availability, processing requirements, and application needs.

items.q: Can SYNC develop a custom rubber formulation?
a: Yes. Our technical resources support evaluating existing compounds, modifying formulations, and developing application-specific materials.

items.q: Can SYNC match an existing rubber compound?
a: SYNC can evaluate existing material specifications, samples, and performance requirements to determine whether an established or newly developed formulation could meet the application.
Exact duplication of a proprietary compound may not be possible without its formulation and processing information.

items.q: Does SYNC support specialized material requirements?
a: Yes. Our material expertise supports applications involving temperature, chemical resistance, electrical performance, hardness, mechanical properties, and other defined requirements.
Any regulatory or material-standard conformance must be evaluated for the specific formulation.

items.q: Can SYNC compound rubber for bonded metal components?
a: Yes. Our rubber compounding and rubber-to-metal bonding capabilities can be coordinated to address the requirements of bonded assemblies.

items.q: Does SYNC support small-batch rubber compounding?
a: Yes. Our established mixing capabilities support smaller-batch rubber formulations, subject to material, equipment, and program requirements.

items.q: What information is needed to request a quote?
a: Useful information includes the intended application, rubber material or specification, required physical properties, operating conditions, estimated volumes, and any existing compound or component samples.
Our team can help evaluate material options when a specific formulation has not been selected.
